Anki as code

Export and reconcile Anki collections as TOML
  • 1: CLI reference

Anki as code exports collections as protobuf-backed TOML, plans changes, and reconciles them through Anki’s native API. It accepts modern .colpkg archives containing collection.anki21b and offline collection databases such as collection.anki2. Keep Anki and other writers closed during export, state operations, apply, and build. Plan, config dump, and state dump use stdout; status and errors use stderr.

Configuration paths identify objects, similar to Terraform. Native IDs live in Anki and collection-backed state; note GUIDs remain Anki metadata. New files create new objects; explicit moves retain existing identities and review progress. Apply/build leave all configuration files unchanged. New notes and their note types can be created in the same apply, without generating or writing identities into source.

Collection operations live under col (alias collection): col export, col plan, col apply, col build, and col state. The namespace flag --state-key belongs to this group. Text-only operations use config (alias conf), such as conf dump. Collection source flags remain specific to each operation: --collection for existing collections and --base for builds.

The CLI reference contains help for all commands, including the generated Anki API tree. Bazel generates this single page from the Cobra definitions with tools/generate_cli_docs and packages it with the documentation; the generated Markdown is not checked in. Build it with bazel_agent bazel build //projects/anki_as_code/docs:cli_reference.

Native server

The Linux x86_64 application links the Rust server into its executable. Collection operations launch the same executable with server serve and communicate over stdio. The installed CLI needs no companion worker, PATH lookup, or executable extraction. bazel_agent bazel build -c opt //projects/anki_as_code produces an optimized executable with final symbol and debug information stripping. It uses the host Linux runtime libraries, including OpenSSL 3.

server shows the available server operations. server run forwards arguments to the linked Rust CLI, which owns native subcommands and their help. server serve invokes App.ServerServe, which delegates to App.ServerRun with serve prepended. Cobra forwards arguments without interpreting native flags:

anki_as_code server run --help
anki_as_code server serve --help
anki_as_code server serve --transport tcp --listen 127.0.0.1:50051
anki_as_code server serve --transport unix --listen ./anki.sock

Stdio is the default and reserves stdout for gRPC. TCP and Unix listeners use plaintext gRPC and require an explicit address. The child process keeps native failures and shutdown separate from the application workflow.

Upstream API commands

api <service> <method> constructs its command tree from the compiled Go protobuf descriptors for all 25 pinned Anki schemas. Bazel automatically generates the registration imports into internal/rpc from the pinned descriptor set using the project-local tools/generate_anki_schemas generator; no separate generation step or runtime schema files are needed. Service/method names use kebab-case, omit the Service suffix and retain backend- prefixes. Implicit backend methods are included. Help lists request fields and message types; no proto files or server discovery are needed.

anki_as_code api tags all-tags --collection ./collection.colpkg
anki_as_code api notes get-note --collection ./collection.anki2 \
  --input request.toml --input-format toml --output-format json
anki_as_code api notes get-note --backend unix:///path/to/anki.sock \
  --input request.json

Exactly one of --collection and --backend is required. Offline access starts the same executable with server serve and owns the collection lifetime. --backend accepts a TCP host:port, tcp://host:port, unix:///absolute/path or an absolute Unix socket path. It uses the server’s current collection and closes only the client connection. Explicit open/close/import RPCs require connected access. Unix URI paths can be relative, such as unix://anki.sock. App resolves methods, validates payloads and owns remote client connections directly; collection.Store manages only offline collection scopes.

Input defaults to stdin (--input -); JSON is the default input and output encoding. An empty request body is accepted for empty request messages. --timeout bounds input reading, startup and the request, defaulting to 30 seconds. Responses use stdout after cleanup succeeds; request, publication and cleanup errors use stderr and a nonzero exit status. Native error details are preserved.

Offline archive write-back is enabled by default. --write-back enables it and --no-write-back disables it; the last occurrence wins. Explicit boolean values such as --write-back=false are also accepted. Disabling write-back skips automatic .colpkg publication; native RPCs keep their normal effects. .anki2 mutations always commit directly. Requests are not transactions: earlier committed changes can persist even when a later RPC fails.

Onboarding an existing collection

Export a full .colpkg from Anki, then close Anki and other collection writers. Use a fresh text directory so stale declarations from earlier exports are not included. Export configs and their native bindings together:

bazel_agent bazel run //projects/anki_as_code -- col export \
  --collection /absolute/path/collection.colpkg --output /absolute/path/text \
  --state-output /absolute/path/state.anki.toml
bazel_agent bazel run //projects/anki_as_code -- col state update \
  --collection /absolute/path/collection.colpkg /absolute/path/state.anki.toml
bazel_agent bazel run //projects/anki_as_code -- config dump \
  --text /absolute/path/text
# Edit the TOML files before planning and applying.
bazel_agent bazel run //projects/anki_as_code -- col plan \
  --collection /absolute/path/collection.colpkg --text /absolute/path/text
bazel_agent bazel run //projects/anki_as_code -- col apply \
  --collection /absolute/path/collection.colpkg --text /absolute/path/text
# Alternatively, build a separate archive instead of applying in place.
bazel_agent bazel run //projects/anki_as_code -- col build \
  --base /absolute/path/collection.colpkg --text /absolute/path/text \
  --output /absolute/path/rebuilt.colpkg

The export leaves collection content and its stored state unchanged; source archives may be repackaged. The optional state file contains version-1 TOML bindings for every exported deck, note and note type, including field/template identities and referenced scheduling preset aliases. It uses the exact generated filenames, including collision suffixes and names retained from the selected state namespace. col state update installs those bindings into the same collection before you edit configs. This preserves existing object identities and review progress when you later apply changes. Use the same --state-key for export, state update, plan, apply and build if selecting a custom namespace.

After editing, inspect col plan, then use col apply to update the supplied collection or col build to write a separate archive. After apply, import the updated archive into Anki; after build, import rebuilt.colpkg. Collection-backed bindings travel with the archive.

Omit --state-output for config-only export. Use col state import for selective manual bindings. Generated state belongs to the collection it was exported from; do not install it into an unrelated collection. State update merges bindings and retains omitted entries; col state replace intentionally removes omitted bindings. For an already managed collection, review exported state before installing it, especially if paths have changed.

--state-output names a TOML file, regardless of its extension. Current-user ~ paths are supported. The file may live outside the text directory or inside it under an unrelated name such as state.anki.toml. Export rejects source aliases, config declaration filenames and directories needed by exported configs. State output is atomically replaced after config export succeeds. Filesystem failures may leave partial configs; a failed config export retains the previous state output. The config tree and state file are not published as one filesystem transaction.

Use absolute paths with bazel run, which can start outside the checkout. Current-user ~ and ~/... paths are supported. --text accepts a collection root file or its directory. config dump defaults to JSON; --format toml is also available. The CLI starts its linked server through its own executable path. No Python is required.

Configuration-set export

config export [FILE] --output DIRECTORY writes a serialized CollectionConfigSet as the fixed TOML hierarchy. Input defaults to JSON; --format toml accepts a TOML-encoded config set. Omit FILE or use - to read stdin. The conf alias works for both dump and export. These commands operate without opening Anki.

anki_as_code config dump --text ./configs > configs.json
anki_as_code config export configs.json --output ./copy
anki_as_code config dump --text ./configs | anki_as_code config export --output ./copy

The caller supplies complete configs with valid, unique collection-relative paths. Schema decoding happens before writes; collection semantics and path validation remain the caller’s responsibility. Export overwrites declared files and retains unrelated entries. Filesystem failures can leave partial output; callers can export to a temporary directory when they need staged publication. Status goes to stderr and stdout stays empty.

App.ConfigExport(ctx, output, configs) exposes the same writer for Go callers through config.Store.Export, without changing the supplied protobuf object.

State operations

State commands accept an existing offline .anki2 database or .colpkg archive through --collection. Commands call App’s typed state workflows. App borrows one prepared connection from collection.Store, which reserves the source and constructs the native worker and collection backends. Collection cleanup finishes before transport cleanup and source reservation release. State stores borrow the connection and own no native lifetime or files.

Databases are opened directly and committed writes persist in place, including when a later operation fails. Packages are restored into a temporary directory and written back during cleanup through Anki’s atomic package API, including media. Publication runs independently of request outcomes and may repackage unchanged content. Normal cleanup removes restored files; publication failures or uncertain native completion follow the backend library’s retention/error contract.

Missing files and non-regular inputs fail before startup. Anki validates package contents during restore. Cleanup uses a bounded context independent of command cancellation, and operation and cleanup errors are preserved. Keep Anki and other writers closed during these operations. Collection export and reconciliation use the same native workflow.

anki_as_code col state dump --collection /path/to/collection.anki2 > state.anki.toml
anki_as_code col state import --collection /path/to/collection.anki2 --text /path/to/configs \
  decks/Default/deck.anki.toml=1 notes/example.note.anki.toml=123
anki_as_code col state update --collection /path/to/collection.anki2 state.anki.toml
anki_as_code col state replace --collection /path/to/collection.anki2 state.anki.toml

Dump returns stored bindings without writes or discovery. An absent namespace returns empty version-1 state. TOML is the default; --format json selects JSON. Update and replace read FILE or stdin when omitted/-. Status and errors use stderr; dump uses stdout.

Import accepts multiple PATH=ID arguments, resolves declared config paths before interpreting native identifiers, checks the requested existing objects and saves once after the complete batch succeeds. IDs remain strings at the CLI/Go API boundary; Anki currently requires positive int64 IDs. Note-type imports include native field/template bindings. Existing scheduling presets use presets/<alias> addresses. Import does not edit config files or native objects.

Update merges external version-1 state: omitted map keys remain, supplied keys replace their complete entry, including note-type member maps. Replace installs the whole object and removes omitted bindings. It can repair invalid saved state; invalid replacement input and native read failures still fail before writing. Validation rejects conflicting path/native ownership before writes. Empty updates and identical operations perform no state write. Native notes, cards, scheduling, history, presets and media remain owned by Anki.

Missing or unknown state subcommands fail with nonzero status and stderr output. Explicit col state --help succeeds.

--state-key KEY selects a namespace; the default is anki_as_code/state/v1. Only that key is written. Callers coordinate concurrent writes to the same key. State uses separate typed maps under State.Resources:

version = "1"
[resources.decks."decks/Default/deck.anki.toml"]
id = "1"
[resources.notes."notes/example.note.anki.toml"]
id = "123"
[resources.note_types."note_types/Basic.notetype.anki.toml"]
id = "456"
[resources.note_types."note_types/Basic.notetype.anki.toml".fields.Front]
id = "789"
[resources.presets.Default]
id = "1"

api/ankiascodeapi provides ankiascodeapi.App, the shared interface for configuration, collection, state and server workflows. pkg/ankiascode provides the concrete ankiascode.App. Its zero value supports configuration operations and borrowed connections. Path sources require explicit worker configuration; hosting the server requires an injected ServerRunner. ankiascode.New(ankiascode.Options{BackendBinary: path, BackendArguments: args}) configures an explicit worker executable and arguments. The CLI supplies its own executable and []string{"server", "serve"}. Operations follow the CLI namespaces: ConfigDump, ConfigExport, ColExport, ColPlan, ColApply, ColBuild, and ColStateDump, ColStateImport, ColStateUpdate, ColStateReplace, ServerRun and ServerServe. Each collection operation accepts an ankiascodeapi.CollectionSource from api/ankiascodeapi: a path described by CollectionPath(path) or an already-open connection described by CollectionConnection(connection). Exactly one alternative must be present. Constructors perform no I/O. ColBuild continues accepting a base archive path because it stages and opens an independent copy.

internal/cli owns the complete Cobra tree, flags, binding syntax, formats and streams. Every operation, including server run and server serve, goes through ankiascodeapi.App. The interface uses shared source types, strings, protobuf messages and standard-library types. Commands wrap collection path flags without opening resources. App owns server delegation and composes collection/configuration workflows; the lower-level packages retain their domain and lifecycle responsibilities. CLI does not host native code or construct App.

cmd/anki_as_code constructs App and passes it to cli.New. It injects the linked ankiserver.Run adapter through Options.ServerRunner and supplies process signal handling. App.ServerRun checks startup cancellation, builds the native argument vector and invokes that adapter. Native serving owns the process until return or termination; its context controls entry only. App does not link Rust/cgo or change process-global signals. Missing runner configuration fails before native hosting. Isolated command tests supply one fake without constructing App or starting Anki. Commands pass namespaces explicitly, and App retains no command configuration.

var application ankiascodeapi.App = ankiascode.New(ankiascode.Options{BackendBinary: serverPath, BackendArguments: []string{"serve"}})
source := ankiascodeapi.CollectionPath(absoluteCollectionPath)
// ConfigDump(ctx, path, format) works without a native backend.
value, err := application.ColStateDump(ctx, source, key)
err = application.ColStateImport(ctx, source, absoluteConfigPath, key, bindings)
err = application.ColStateUpdate(ctx, source, key, external)
err = application.ColStateReplace(ctx, source, key, replacement)

App’s path-based operations return after cleanup. Borrowed connections remain owned by their caller, including after failure or cancellation. Operations read fresh collection data and neither close the borrowed connection nor publish a package. Callers coordinate access and decide when to save and close; direct database writes persist immediately and multiple calls are not a transaction. One App can alternate between several open collections:

first := ankiascodeapi.CollectionConnection(firstConnection)
second := ankiascodeapi.CollectionConnection(secondConnection)
err := application.ColStateUpdate(ctx, first, key, external)
report, err := application.ColPlan(ctx, first, absoluteConfigPath, key)
other, err := application.ColStateDump(ctx, second, key)

The protobuf contract lives in api/ankiascodepb, with Go package ankiascodepb and protobuf namespace anki_as_code. Message names and fields retain the existing config and state formats; Go imports and protobuf fully qualified type names use the renamed API.

ColExport(ctx, source, output, stateOutput, stateKey) accepts an empty stateOutput for config-only export or a TOML file path for snapshot bindings. For a borrowed connection, its owner must keep both outputs distinct from native collection files: a connection source carries no filename for alias checks. Config/state output conflict checks still apply.

internal/collection.Store reserves existing sources and owns enabled archive publication. Construct it with explicit process options before collection access. WithCollection injects a prepared grpc.ClientConnInterface into its callback. Construct the services you need on that connection and reuse local instances for several operations.

collection.New(collection.Options{Backend: ankiclient.BackendSTDOptions{Binary: path, Arguments: args}}) configures the worker. No executable or server arguments are discovered by default; missing configuration fails before opening a collection. Callers supply their server executable and runtime inputs. Each scope constructs a fresh stdin/stdout worker and collection backend. It closes native storage before stopping the worker. Collection publication and close have a ten-minute default budget, configurable with Options.CollectionCloseTimeout; transport cleanup has a separate five-second budget independent of callback cancellation; source reservations outlive cleanup.

store := collection.New(collection.Options{Backend: ankiclient.BackendSTDOptions{Binary: serverPath, Arguments: []string{"serve"}}})
err := store.WithCollection(ctx, collection.CollectionOptions{Path: path, WriteBack: true}, func(connection grpc.ClientConnInterface) (bool, error) {
    resources := resource.New(connection)
    states := state.New(connection, key)
    exporter := export.New(resources, states)
    if err := exporter.Export(ctx, directory, ""); err != nil {
        return false, fmt.Errorf("export configs: %w", err)
    }
    changed, err := states.Replace(ctx, replacement)
    if err != nil {
        return false, fmt.Errorf("replace bindings: %w", err)
    }
    return changed, nil
})

Callbacks finish all work sequentially before returning. Retained connections reject calls after cleanup. Resource/state stores and exporters borrow the connection; each operation reads fresh data. A Store or App must not be copied after use. Duplicate canonical paths and file aliases are rejected within one Store; callers coordinate access across different stores and external writers.

CollectionOptions selects the source path and WriteBack policy. Enabled write-back publishes the source archive during cleanup independently of callback results, errors and cancellation. Application workflows explicitly enable it; API flags select it. Database writes persist immediately, including before later errors; the scope is not a transaction. To export another archive destination, use Anki’s ExportCollectionPackage with the injected connection as the final operation and disable WriteBack when source publication is unwanted. Native export consumes the open collection; backend cleanup handles it.

App.APICall(ctx, ankiascodeapi.APIRequest{...}) exposes the same generic operation without per-method wrappers. Supply a fully qualified gRPC Method, Input bytes and JSON/TOML encodings. Collection accepts the shared path or borrowed-connection source; Backend selects an app-owned connection to a running server. Exactly one is required. WriteBack defaults to false for Go callers; the CLI explicitly selects true. Borrowed native connections retain caller-owned cleanup and publication. Request validation precedes native startup.

State Go API

internal/state borrows a prepared connection and owns no process, collection lifecycle or files. The selected namespace defaults when the key is empty:

store := state.New(connection, "")
value, err := store.Dump(ctx)
changed, err := store.Import(ctx, configs, map[string]string{
    "notes/example.note.anki.toml": "123",
})
changed, err = store.Update(ctx, external)
changed, err = store.Replace(ctx, replacement)

Dump, Update and Replace exchange *ankiascodepb.State. Import accepts a parsed *ankiascodepb.CollectionConfigSet and path/ID strings. Multiple calls reuse the same prepared connection. The changed flag reports whether state was written. State.Resources groups typed deck, note, note-type and preset maps; note types own field/template maps.

state.Export(configs, snapshot, identities) generates version-1 bindings from projected configs, their path-to-native-ID map and the same native snapshot. State owns construction and validation of resource and member bindings, including scheduling preset aliases. This pure operation performs no backend calls and installs no state. Collection export owns config paths and file output.

Collection lifecycle

For path sources, App delegates native access to collection.Store.WithCollection. The store reserves the source and constructs BackendSTD and BackendCollection, using only the explicitly configured executable and arguments. BackendCollection restores packages into temporary storage or opens databases directly. Callbacks receive the prepared connection and construct their own services. Store closes the collection before stopping the worker, including after callback errors, cancellation and panic unwinding.

BackendCollection owns readiness, native import/open/close and restore cleanup. Its failure contract can retain restore files when native completion is uncertain, reporting their path. The CLI and App add no restore owner or lifecycle state machine.

Store reserves each source before startup and retains that reservation through cleanup. When WriteBack is enabled, BackendCollection publishes its source archive through Anki independently of callback outcomes. Anki writes and atomically replaces that archive. Database operations persist in place. Build separately copies its base to a temporary directory beside the destination, applies to that copy and atomically replaces the destination after success. Failed builds remove staging and leave the destination untouched. Callers own exclusive access to the base and destination. State, export and reconciliation borrow prepared services without owning lifetime.

Export and explicit moves

Export writes configuration TOML without changing the source collection. --state-output optionally writes matching snapshot bindings for onboarding. Existing stored bindings retain note and note-type filenames on re-export. New note types receive unused filenames with numeric suffixes when their names collide with tracked paths, including case-only differences and fallback names. Without bindings, native edits can change content-derived filenames.

Export selects a note’s directory from its first regular card. Card generation or changed destinations can therefore change an exported path, including when Anki chooses a deck for a new root note. When adopting these new paths, declare [[moved]] entries from their stored paths before applying. Export does not rewrite bindings. Applying the same root-note configs again preserves native identity and converges; Anki owns their initial deck selection.

Follow onboarding to bind the whole export before the first reconciliation, or use col state import for selective bindings. New configs without bindings describe new objects. State dump exports stored bindings separately; it does not discover bindings for an untracked config tree:

bazel_agent bazel run //projects/anki_as_code -- col state dump \
  --collection /absolute/path/collection.colpkg > /absolute/path/state.anki.toml

Export writes declared files directly through config.Store.Export and does not reload generated files. Other entries remain untouched, including old configs and state files other than an explicit --state-output destination. The destination must not contain the source collection. Filesystem errors may leave partial output.

Use a fresh destination for a clean snapshot. For directory cleanup or synchronization, export to a temporary directory and use rsync or another external tool; those policies belong to the caller.

To rename or move a resource without replacing it, move its file/directory and add a root [[moved]] pair. Directory moves include descendant notes/decks; type moves include their members. Fields/templates use addresses such as note_types/Basic.notetype.anki.toml#fields/Front. Update readable references in the same edit. Moves require independent, nonoverlapping endpoints, reject occupied destinations, and are idempotent when retained. The old source must no longer be declared. Remove a completed move before reusing its old path.

Managed and unmanaged entities

  • Notes: add/remove tracked notes; edit exact named fields and tags shared by their generated cards. Only tracked notes missing from configs are removed.
  • Regular-deck assignments: move generated cards using note defaults and template/cloze ordinals. Card entries assign decks and do not declare existence. Before deleting a deck containing retained cards, declare a surviving destination for them. An omitted assignment keeps the card and its existing deck.
  • Decks: create, rename/move, remove, and edit normal or filtered configuration. Titles derive from the fixed hierarchy. A deck must be empty in Anki before conversion between normal and filtered kinds. Native APIs must support the requested removal; required native objects cannot silently become untracked.
  • Note types: create, rename, remove, and edit ordered fields, templates, CSS, browser fonts, and upstream presentation settings. Explicit member moves preserve field/template identities. Edit affected named note fields together. Existing notes cannot switch to another native note type through this CLI.

These are excluded from editable desired state:

  • Resident filtered cards: membership, home decks, and temporary scheduling belong to Anki. Their assignments are omitted. Empty the filtered deck before removing referenced resources or changing a resident card’s template structure.
  • Scheduling presets: referenced by readable names; never created, deleted, or edited. The CLI calls no preset-writing API.
  • Existing card scheduling/state and review history: preserved in the database to retain study progress. Anki initializes cards it generates for new notes/templates.
  • Media payloads: preserved through Anki’s native package APIs. Field references are editable; media creation/deletion is outside the workflow.
  • Collection/UI/sync settings and native metadata: owned by Anki and omitted from text. API operations update their normal bookkeeping as needed.
  • Untracked objects: preserved during apply. Import them before edits that would destroy their references, such as deleting a deck with untracked cards, renaming a parent with untracked children, or changing shared field/card structure.

Publication and planning

Plan reads an API snapshot, resolves config references and moves, checks owned relationships, and compares requested resources in memory. It performs no native mutations, writes no bindings and creates no database copy. It reports paths, resource changes and known card deck assignments. card_generation_deferred indicates that Anki determines generated-card effects during apply; the planner does not claim exact creation/removal counts for those effects.

Anki performs final template validation, normalization and card generation during apply. Planning can therefore accept a template that apply rejects. Source values that Anki normalizes can remain different from stored values in subsequent plans; accepted values are never written back into TOML.

Database apply updates the supplied collection directly. Anki commits each native operation, so later errors can leave earlier operations committed. Archive apply uses Anki’s atomic package export during cleanup. Earlier committed changes can persist after later request failures; read operations may repackage unchanged content. Build requires a distinct archive output and stages its copy before Apply, publishing the completed archive atomically after success. Keep other writers closed while using a collection; the CLI does not detect concurrent archive replacement.

Collection export writes its declared config files in place. It does not traverse, clean or replace the destination directory. Other entries remain untouched, and filesystem errors may leave partial output. Callers can export to a temporary directory and synchronize it externally when required. Converged database apply leaves source bytes unchanged. Note-type comparison ignores runtime ordinal hints and unmanaged metadata while retaining explicit field/template identity changes. New notes use Anki’s batch creation API. Export neither writes source state nor produces a state file. Failed native reads or projection leave existing output unchanged.

Fixed hierarchy

collection.anki.toml
note_types/
  Basic.notetype.anki.toml
notes/
  unattached.note.anki.toml
decks/
  Languages/
    deck.anki.toml
    notes/
      introduction.note.anki.toml
    decks/
      French/
        deck.anki.toml
        notes/
          greeting.note.anki.toml

The root contains version, currently 1. Optional moves describe file, directory, or nested definition address changes for reconciliation:

version = "1"
[[moved]]
from = 'decks/Old'
to = 'decks/Languages'

decks/Languages/decks/French/ declares Languages::French. Every deck directory requires deck.anki.toml. Titles come from the hierarchy and are absent from markers. A normal deck references an existing scheduling preset by readable name:

preset = 'Default'
[normal]
description = 'Language lessons'

Notes reference note types by configuration path and contain exact named fields:

note_type = 'note_types/Basic.notetype.anki.toml'
[fields]
Front = 'Bonjour'
Back = 'Hello'
[[cards]]
ordinal = "0"

An omitted card deck inherits its declaring deck’s marker path. Explicit card and template overrides use paths such as decks/Languages/deck.anki.toml. Note types declare names, upstream configuration, ordered fields and templates. sort_field selects a field by name; template target_deck references a deck path. Array order determines field/template positions.

Paths identify resources. Editable configs contain no top-level Anki IDs or note GUIDs. A note at a new path declares a new resource; identity-preserving moves belong in the root’s moved list. Explicit state operations install bindings inside the collection; export writes configs only. The identity generation command has been removed.

The loader lists immediate files in notes/ and note_types/, descending only through child decks/. Other files and deeper note directories are ignored. Missing resource directories are empty sets. Empty markers are parseable; business logic determines whether they are usable. Symlinks, non-directory resource roots, and missing deck markers fail.

The format is unreleased and stays version 1 while the schema evolves. Only the current schema is supported. Normal/filtered settings and note-type presentation reuse Anki messages. Native-only fields in reused messages are omitted by collection export and rejected by reconciliation; pure dump/export retains supplied protobuf values without semantic checks.

Serialization and package APIs

These operations work with configuration files and protobuf objects without opening Anki. Load checks syntax, schema, version, and filesystem layout; callers own collection semantics. Dump calls Load and serializes the complete parsed set. Export can write a caller-supplied object directly without loading it first. Read, encoding, and filesystem failures end the operation with an error. Export may leave partial output; it does not validate relationships or clean up files.

The class diagram shows root and resource configuration messages. References use paths; card and template deck references target normal decks. Each note stores shared field content and tags, while note types define ordered fields, templates, and presentation. The root marker contains the version and explicit moves. Attached notes identify each file’s location in the fixed hierarchy. In Load, each file is decoded as it is read, and deck titles and omitted card deck paths are derived inside the deck loop. Dump selects JSON or TOML encoding for the complete configuration set.

TOML decodes to generic values, then JSON, then protobuf using ProtoJSON. Unknown keys and incompatible values fail. Unquoted TOML dates/times fail rather than silently becoming strings; quote dates used as note text. Output converts ProtoJSON directly to TOML, preserving optional presence and exact text values. 64-bit values use quoted decimal strings, including version = "1".

config.New(root) returns a *config.Store bound to a configuration path without accessing the filesystem. Use a directory for writing; reads also accept a root config file. The store exposes:

  • Load() (*ankiascodepb.CollectionConfigSet, error) parses the hierarchy.
  • Dump(format string) ([]byte, error) loads and encodes JSON or TOML.
  • Export(configs *ankiascodepb.CollectionConfigSet) error writes the root marker and supplied path/config pairs as TOML files beneath its directory.
store := config.New(absoluteDirectory)
configs, err := store.Load()
data, err := store.Dump("json")
err = store.Export(configs)

Stores retain no parsed messages or open files. Each Load reads fresh values; callers own filesystem coordination and the returned messages. config.Version supplies the supported schema version to collection exporters.

Export writes directly, preserves input messages, overwrites declared files, and leaves unrelated/stale files alone. Callers own valid, unique paths, layout, validation, staging, cleanup, and publication. Export does not load or normalize its output; failures may leave partial files. Consumers use the store; the layout package remains an implementation API with restricted Bazel visibility.

config/layout owns the fixed hierarchy, discovery, file I/O, and direct file export. internal/codec converts TOML/JSON through protobuf without filesystem access. Config layout, config dump, state CLI commands, and collection export reuse its format dispatch; TOML/JSON helpers are private. Dependencies flow from config to layout/codec and from layout to codec. State stores have no serialization dependency. Collection relationship validation and native operations remain outside them.

Architecture

The outer box shows the executable’s components: the CLI, App, and the linked Rust server library. The CLI invokes App, which reads and writes text Configs. Run (C ABI) invokes the library through the injected server runner. Path-based workflows launch another instance of anki_as_code as a server subprocess and use gRPC over stdio to communicate with its Server. The Server delegates storage operations to the Anki API. Both server variants access Anki storage, which holds native resources and the application’s persisted state.

The external-server gRPC edge is used by api --backend with an explicit TCP or Unix address. App owns only its client connection. Go callers can also prepare external connections through ankiclient.BackendGRPC and pass them to App through ankiascodeapi.CollectionConnection.

Package dependencies

The project keeps one Go module with focused packages. Configs and state are protobuf contracts. Runtime resolution models stay private to internal/plan; packages expose only operations used by their consumers.

Each package’s doc.go describes its responsibilities and boundaries; this diagram shows how the packages compose.

Dotted edges show calls through injected contracts. Solid edges show component dependencies.

Package Responsibility
cmd/anki_as_code App construction, CLI invocation and process signals
internal/cli Cobra commands, application dispatch and streams
internal/collection Source reservations and archive publication
api/ankiascodepb Generated config, plan, and persisted-state contracts
api/ankiascodeapi Shared application interface and collection source contracts
pkg/ankiascode Application workflows and service composition
internal/export Native-to-config projection and direct file output
internal/plan Pure resolution, comparison, ownership and prepared operations
internal/reconcile Execute protobuf plans, bind native IDs and persist state
internal/rebuild Apply to a staged archive copy and publish it atomically
internal/resource Native generated clients and fresh resource snapshots
internal/config Root-bound configuration Store for Load, Dump, and Export
internal/config/layout Fixed hierarchy, discovery, file I/O, and direct export
internal/rpc Compiled upstream descriptor catalog and protobuf RPC execution
internal/codec Filesystem-independent protobuf/TOML/JSON conversion
internal/state Stored-state dump, import, update, and replacement

The command entry point injects App into internal/cli through ankiascodeapi.App, checking compatibility during compilation. Commands use the shared interface without importing the implementation. Shared API types do not depend on native backend ownership. App obtains a prepared connection from the supplied source and constructs its services locally. Path sources use collection.Store; borrowed sources retain caller-owned lifetime. export.New(resources, states) constructs an Exporter using caller-provided resource and state stores. Its Export(ctx, output) method owns native-to-config projection, filenames and direct config output. State operations remain separate. Export has no dependency on reconciliation.

plan.Build(configs, snapshot, stored) constructs prepared protobuf operations without I/O. reconcile.New(resources, states) constructs a Reconciler whose Apply(ctx, compiled) method executes them and returns whether native data or bindings changed. App shares config loading, capture and plan preparation between plan and apply within one collection scope. Planning owns reference resolution, comparison and ownership; execution owns native calls and returned identities.

Config and codec have no Anki runtime dependency. State owns stored path bindings, not lifecycle or serialization. App uses the Go backends in projects/anki_grpc and Anki’s collection/package services; Resource owns generated resource clients and fresh native snapshots. The executor borrows resource/state stores and owns no process or filesystem resources. There is no archive facade or handwritten ZIP/Zstandard handling. Anki owns storage compatibility, normalization, structural migrations, field caches, and card generation. No HTML cache rebuilding or SQLite driver is implemented in Go. The application does not force Check Database after import; normal Anki API updates maintain their caches.

Planning Go API

plan.Build(configs, snapshot, stored) returns an executable protobuf CollectionPlan from caller-supplied configs, a resource snapshot and stored bindings. It performs no I/O and leaves all inputs unchanged. Callers capture fresh inputs under exclusive offline access to the same collection and namespace. Backend lifetime belongs to the caller; planning can run with the backend open or closed.

The plan separates expected_state from proposed_bindings and contains a change report, prepared deck/type/note operations, name releases, tracked deletions and card destinations. New objects have zero native IDs; prepared note-type and template-deck references use configuration paths. Resource comparison produces operations and report entries together. Converged plans have no native operations. Card destinations are included only for known changes or relevant native generation. Planning indexes native protobufs directly and resolves desired configs into the prepared protobufs used for comparison and execution. Returned payloads are independent of supplied inputs; path/ID indexes and ownership checks stay private to internal/plan. Member moves rename fields or templates within one note type; cross-type identity transfers are rejected. Stable native member IDs are authoritative. Without IDs, matching uses original stored names, including before explicit renames; stale ordinals cannot claim another current member. Ambiguous bindings fail before a plan is returned. Untracked resources and resident filtered cards stay unmanaged, including deck targets referenced by untracked templates. All cloze card ordinals share template zero; resident cards block template replacement or removal, while explicit template moves that preserve identity remain allowed.

Anki owns native validation, normalization, structural migrations and card generation. The report compares current card destinations and cards removed with deleted notes; template-driven additions, removals and migrations remain deferred through card_generation_deferred. Prepared operations do not simulate those native effects. The CLI and App’s ColPlan return the report; Go services pass the complete plan to reconcile.New(resources, states).Apply(ctx, compiled).

The executor checks expected stored state before writes, executes prepared operations, resolves new native IDs and persists bindings. It never loads configs, captures a resource snapshot, matches members or recomputes the plan. Native metadata and newly generated cards are read only as needed to execute it. A private applier reads the supplied plan unchanged, clones the proposed bindings, and copies only note-type requests whose native identities or presentation need updating. Reports, expected state and note bodies are not cloned. Callers retain exclusive access and own freshness beyond stored-state checks.

compiled, err := plan.Build(configs, snapshot, stored)
changed, err := reconcile.New(resources, states).Apply(ctx, compiled)

Archive build Go API

internal/rebuild stages a separate collection archive using an injected apply operation:

builder := rebuild.New(apply)
err := builder.Build(ctx, baseArchive, outputArchive)

The non-nil callback receives a private .colpkg path and must finish all native work and close its session before returning. Builder knows nothing about configs, Anki clients or reconciliation. Callers own home-path expansion and exclusive source/destination access; the destination parent must already exist.

Builder checks the regular source file and rejects source/destination aliases, copies into a private directory beside the destination, then publishes the completed archive with an atomic rename. Apply errors, cancellation observed before publication and publication failures leave the original and existing destination intact. Staging is removed on return, including panic unwinding; cleanup errors are retained. Cancellation preserves both the context error and its custom cause for errors.Is. Atomic publication does not guarantee power-loss durability. The App callback delegates to ColApply.

Run bazel_agent bazel test //projects/anki_as_code/internal/rebuild:rebuild_test. The native E2E changes real Anki state in the staged archive and emits original, changed and unchanged .colpkg files plus a decoded JSON state object.

Native resource Go API

internal/resource shares generated native clients and complete snapshots on a caller-owned prepared connection:

resources := resource.New(connection)
snapshot, err := resources.Snapshot(ctx)
note, err := resources.Notes.GetNote(ctx, &notes.NoteId{Nid: noteID})

Store exposes the generated deck, note-type, note, card, search, preset and rendering clients without forwarding wrappers. Snapshot returns upstream protobuf objects, including unmanaged resources and resident filtered cards, plus preset names. Decks are ordered by title; note types, notes and cards by native ID. Each call reads fresh values and returns caller-owned results. There is no cache or atomic snapshot guarantee; callers provide exclusive offline access.

The resource store owns no backend lifecycle, state bindings, configs, projection, planning or mutation order. Export and reconciliation retain those policies. No SQL or duplicate storage logic is involved.

Collection export Go API

internal/export borrows resource and state stores for the same prepared collection:

resources := resource.New(connection)
states := state.New(connection, key)
exporter := export.New(resources, states)
err := exporter.Export(ctx, absoluteOutputDirectory, absoluteStateFile)

Stored bindings retain filenames and preset aliases. Export(ctx, directory, stateFile) writes configs and optional bindings from the same snapshot as TOML. An empty state destination selects config-only behavior. Export never installs state; state operations remain separate. The destination must not contain the source collection.

New note filenames use Anki’s HtmlToTextLine result for the configured sort field. Go only sanitizes that text into a bounded Unicode filename. Bound names are reused from state; filename conversion never changes stored note fields.

Export owns config projection and readable filenames and delegates file output to config.Store.Export. It overwrites declared configs in place and leaves other entries untouched, including stale configs and caller-owned state files. Filesystem errors may leave partial output. For cleanup or publication policies, export to a temporary directory and synchronize it externally, for example with rsync. The caller also owns exclusive offline access, backend startup, collection preparation and shutdown.

Export and reconciliation share resource.Store for generated clients and fresh native snapshots; their projection and policy remain separate.

Anki backend API

The reusable Go backend and Rust server belong to projects/anki_grpc. The Go package owns the server process and exposes a managed gRPC connection. Callers use Anki’s generated service clients for typed methods. Anki owns collection validation, note updates, card generation, and persistence; this CLI owns TOML and reconciliation.

Integration approaches considered

Direct storage editing has the simplest integration: an application edits SQLite and protobuf itself, taking responsibility for Anki’s data invariants and business logic. The API-based approaches are Python with Anki’s official SDK, Rust with Anki’s Rust API, and another language with a translation layer around the Rust API. The two Rust API approaches require building Anki from source. A translation layer can be a C ABI or a gRPC sidecar; it does not remove that build requirement.

This project uses a translation layer: the Go CLI calls the Rust server in projects/anki_grpc, which forwards operations to Anki’s Rust API. Go owns the server process and its failures.

The maintained Mermaid source is rendered by the :backend_approaches Bazel target and published with the project documentation.

Verification

bazel_agent bazel build //projects/anki_as_code
bazel_agent bazel test //projects/anki_as_code/pkg/ankiascode:ankiascode_test \
  //projects/anki_as_code/internal/export:export_test \
  //projects/anki_as_code/internal/config:store_test \
  //projects/anki_as_code/internal/cli:command_test \
  //projects/anki_as_code/cmd/anki_as_code:cli_workflow_test

Synthetic native E2E verifies reviewed-card/history/preset/media retention, filtered cards, field/template migrations, copied notes, config-only export and independent state operations, import/moves, untracked-object safety, read-only configs, convergence, rejected publication, large fields/archives, and Anki’s actual full-package round trip. CLI E2E verifies streams, flags, removed generation, and pure config behavior. Repeatable TOML, JSON, and collection artifacts are emitted through Bazel’s undeclared test outputs. Exact-candidate delivery receipts own validation status.

The independent exporter E2E uses a caller-managed native backend and collection. It checks exact Unicode/multiline fields, presentation, member bindings, stable bound/discovered paths, native filename text conversion, filtered-card exclusion, read-only state namespaces, untouched existing entries, cancellation and partial output after filesystem errors. It emits a complete text tree and a native .colpkg artifact. Run bazel_agent bazel test //projects/anki_as_code/internal/export:export_test.

anki_as_code col

Inspect and manage Anki collections

Usage:
  anki_as_code col [flags]
  anki_as_code col [command]

Aliases:
  col, collection

Available Commands:
  apply       Reconcile an offline collection in place
  build       Build a new archive from the original and desired text
  export      Export a collection to editable TOML
  plan        Inspect desired collection changes
  state       Inspect and manage collection-backed path bindings

Flags:
  -h, --help               help for col
      --state-key string   Collection state namespace key (default "anki_as_code/state/v1")

Use "anki_as_code col [command] --help" for more information about a command.

      --collection string   Anki .colpkg archive or offline .anki2 database
  -h, --help                help for apply
      --text string         Collection root config or its containing directory

Global Flags:
      --state-key string   Collection state namespace key (default "anki_as_code/state/v1")

      --state-key string   Collection state namespace key (default "anki_as_code/state/v1")
